title: Who writes and reads WAL
caption: A backend copies records into wal_buffers and flushes them to pg_wal at COMMIT, while the walwriter, archiver, checkpointer and startup process each handle one job around the segment files.

title: INSERT and COMMIT to recovery
caption: Follow the numbers: the client only waits for steps 1 to 4, and the archiving, checkpoint and crash replay steps happen later in the background.

badges.meaning: Code builds a WAL record with XLogBeginInsert and XLogRegisterData
XLogInsertRecord copies the record into wal_buffers
COMMIT adds a commit record and calls XLogFlush
WAL is written and fsynced to the pg_wal segment, then the client gets OK
A full segment gets a .ready file in archive_status
The archiver runs archive_command and renames the flag to .done
A checkpoint flushes dirty pages and stores the REDO location in pg_control
After a crash the startup process replays WAL from the REDO location

title: Anatomy of a WAL record
caption: A 24 hex digit file name points to a 16MB segment of 8kB pages, and each record inside starts with an XLogRecord header followed by block headers, a data header and the data.
